description: The Integrated Science Laboratory Club represents Whittier College with an international team of students from the United States, Mexico, Sweden, and Denmark. Combining interests in computer science, mathematics, physics, and engineering, we bring diverse perspectives, creativity, and teamwork to solve complex challenges. United by our passion for STEM and innovation, we are proud to represent the Whittier College Poets!
summary:
Inspired by NASA's Abandoned but Not Forgotten challenge, we created a youth-friendly website that brings NASA's retired space equipment and missions back into the spotlight. Developed in just 48-hours, our project combines interactive content, colorful graphics, simple explanations, and cartoon-style videos.

We believe that even though today's kids are growing up surrounded by advanced technology, learning about space should still feel exciting, visual, and fun. Our goal is to turn complex scientific information into stories that young explorers can understand and enjoy.

We didn't set out to build the most advanced technology. Instead, we wanted to be creative, authentic, and use the tools available to us to make learning more human. After all, every great discovery starts with a question. We want kids to ask theirs, look for answers, and let their imagination explore the possibilities!
details:
Our website allows visitors to explore NASA missions and equipment through organized educational pages, interactive content, and visual storytelling. Topics include Surveyor Landers, Apollo Lunar Models, Lunar Roving Vehicles, Pioneer 10 & 11, the Kepler Telescope, and the Ingenuity Helicopter. Each topic helps users understand the technology, its original purpose, and its contribution to space exploration.

We developed the website primarily using HTML and JavaScript in Visual Studio Code (VS Code). We used Gemini occasionally for coding assistance and troubleshooting, while Kling AI helped create our animated educational videos. We also researched NASA's official websites and resources to support the accuracy of our content.

As a team of Whittier College students representing the Integrated Science Club, we decided to challenge ourselves with a last-minute entry during the 48-hour weekend challenge. We divided responsibilities based on our strengths, combining physics research, programming, content development, and visual design.

Our creative approach combines hands-on website development, scientific research, graphic design, and animated storytelling. We considered our audience's reading levels, attention spans, navigation experience, and different learning styles when organizing the content and designing the visuals.

The project benefits young learners by making scientific information easier to explore independently and understand. Our intended impact is to encourage curiosity, critical thinking, and an early interest in STEM while showing how technology, creativity, and teamwork can turn an idea into an educational experience.
